newsitem.title: YEMEN: Five German tourists said seized in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Five German tourists said seized in Yemen.

text.p: Yemeni kidnappers on Wednesday seized five German tourists in the country's southeastern province of Hadramaut, a Yemeni security source told Reuters.

"The kidnappers, who did not identify themselves, telephoned local authorities and asked them for a 12 million mark ($7 million) ransom to release them," the source said without giving further details.
German embassy officials declined any comment.
An American oil engineer kidnapped by a Yemeni mountain tribe and held for 16 days was released on February 26.

His kidnappers had demanded compensation of $2 million or the return of a piece of land in Sanaa which they said was given to one of their tribal leaders. It was not clear whether their demands had been met in return for the engineer's release.

Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil companies have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips. The hostages were all released unharmed.
